CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA
ORAL ORDER

Petitioners/accused Nos.10 and 11 are knocking at the doors of this Court, in the subject petition,
calling in question continuation of proceedings in C.C.No.131 of 2013 arising out of crime No.294 of 2010 registered for offences punishable under Sections 399, 400 and 114 of the IPC.
2. Heard Sri K B K Swamy, learned counsel appearing for petitioners and Sri Rashmi Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent.

Facts in brief germane are as follows:
Petitioners along with others get embroiled in a crime in crime No.294 of 2010 for offence punishable under Sections 399, 400 and 114 of the IPC.
The police, after investigation, file a charge sheet for the aforesaid offence on 01-02-2011.
The petitioners, at the relevant point in time, were not available for trial.

Therefore,
the concerned Court draws a split charge against these petitioners and tries the other accused, who were available for trial.
By an order dated 06-08-2016 the concerned Court acquits all the accused of the offence in S.C.No.67 of 2013 except these two petitioners, on the score that they were not available for trial.
The trial is now sought to be continued against these petitioners in C.C.No.131 of 2013.

sentences.text: The continuation of the trial is what has driven these petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.

4. Learned counsel for petitioners submits that the reasons so rendered by the concerned Court to acquit all the other accused would undoubtedly enure to the benefit of the petitioners, as the offence is the one of preparation for commission of dacoity under Section 399 of the IPC.

Per-contra, learned High Court Government Pleader would refute the submission contending that the petitioners also must come out clean in a full blown trial as others have come out and no indulgence should be shown to the persons who have escaped trial.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The issue would be whether the petition should be entertained for quashment of the proceedings at the instance of the petitioners who have escaped trial.
8. In the normal circumstances, the petitioners ought to have come out clean in a full blown trial.
However, the reasons rendered by the concerned Court would undoubtedly enure to the benefit of the petitioners, as it is an act committed together i.e., preparation for commission of dacoity.

If the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the guilt against other accused NC: 2024:KHC:51275 beyond all reasonable doubt, it cannot be said that based on the same evidence, these two petitioners would get convicted.
Today what is at stake is precious judicial time.

If the petitioners are permitted to be tried despite the fact that other accused have been acquitted, eventually they would get acquitted of the offence,
but the only thing is loss of precious judicial time.
To obviate the said circumstance, I deem it appropriate to entertain the petition and obliterate the crime against the petitioners.

9. The view of mine, in this regard, is fortified by the judgment of this Court dated 02-09-2022 passed in Crl.P.No.7720/2022, which reads as follows:
"4.
The learned Sessions Judge, by his order dated 01.12.2021, acquits accused Nos.1 to 11, 14, 16 to 18 and 21 in S.C.No.103/2018.

At the relevant point in time, when the trial was on, the petitioner was not available for trial, as he was allegedly absconding and a split charge sheet was issued against the petitioner in S.C.No.87/2019 in terms of an order of the learned Sessions Judge dated 10.06.2019.
The continuation of proceedings in S.C.No.87/2019 is what drives the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal petition is hereby allowed.
(ii) Proceedings in C.C.No.1170/2007 pending on the file of Addl. Civil Judge &
JMFC, Bantwal, in Cr.No.130/2006 registered by - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:51275 Bantwal Rural Police Station, is hereby quashed insofar petitioner is concerned.
In view of criminal petition having been disposed of on merits, I.A.No.1/2017 for stay does not survive for consideration and same stands rejected."
Sri. Ravi K B vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175499976/
8
The Co-ordinate Bench was considering a case where the co-accused who had escaped trial had not surrendered or was not arrested by the police.
In the light of the afore-quoted order and the reasons rendered by the Sessions Court in S.C.No.67/2013 qua accused Nos.1, 2, 5, 7 and 8, the petitioners are also entitled to succeed in the subject petition for the very same reasons rendered by this Court supra.
10.
For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
